title: Generator Rotation
story:
SHIFT HANDOVER SHEET, GENERATOR ROOM, initialled I.H.
[ ] gen-alpha: 400 hours without a break, stand it down
[ ] gen-bravo: rested and ready, bring it online
[ ] gen-charlie: crashed overnight, clear out the wreckage

The three generator services were moved into containers last night. Ingrid went to bed after signing the sheet, so the list is yours. Work through it top to bottom. `docker ps -a` shows every container, running or not, and you will need it to see which one is which.
objectives: Stop `gen-alpha` (it must still exist, just not running)
Start `gen-bravo` so that it is running
startingState: `gen-alpha` is running, `gen-bravo` is stopped, and `gen-charlie` has crashed and exited with an error.
hints: Containers move between states: running, stopped, and removed. Each transition has its own command, and a stopped container still shows up in `docker ps -a`.
Three separate verbs do the work: `docker stop`, `docker start` and `docker rm`, each followed by the container name. Removing is not the same thing as stopping.

```bash
docker ps -a
docker stop gen-alpha
docker start gen-bravo
docker rm gen-charlie
docker ps -a
```

commands: docker run -d --name gen-alpha alpine:3.20 sh -c 'trap "exit 0" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'
docker run -d --name gen-bravo alpine:3.20 sh -c 'trap "exit 0" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'
docker run --name gen-charlie alpine:3.20 sh -c 'exit 3' || true

debrief: Stopping is not deleting: a stopped container keeps its filesystem and logs until `docker rm` takes it away for good. Pro tip: `docker container prune` sweeps every stopped container at once, so run it only when nothing in `docker ps -a` still matters.
